reviews.what-soil-is-made-of: Soil's solid matter arrives from two directions. From below, rock formed hot and under pressure meets the cool, wet surface, and physical, chemical and biological weathering take it apart. Feldspars and other silicates turn into clay minerals and iron oxides, while tough quartz survives as sand and silt. From above, plant debris decays into soil organic matter, and climate decides how much of it builds up. The two meet on clay and oxide surfaces, which bind organic molecules for centuries.
